title: The climb
lede: Anthropic’s route from a 2021 startup to a 2026 IPO, drawn as a mountain. Height is company value: every gridline up is ten times higher than the one below. Tap any flag to see that stage.
notes: Valuations before Series E are press estimates; Anthropic didn’t announce them, and Series D details vary by source.
The IPO is scheduled, not complete: price and timing can still change.

camps.name: Series A
camps.story: Founded by former OpenAI researchers. Their reputation let them start with an unusually large first round and no seed stage.
camps.play: Most startups first raise a few million in seed money to prove people want the product, then a Series A to build a repeatable business.

camps.name: Series B
camps.story: The lead investor’s crypto exchange collapsed months later, and its stake was eventually sold to other investors.
camps.play: Series B is about scaling once the model works: hiring fast and growing revenue. It’s often where a company passes $1B (a unicorn).

camps.name: Series C
camps.lead: Spark Capital, with Google, Salesforce and Zoom
camps.story: Arrived two months after Claude launched publicly. The valuation barely moved since Series B: the steep part of the climb hadn’t started yet.
camps.play: Series C funds market leadership: new products, expansion and acquisitions. New kinds of investors begin to appear.

camps.label: Big tech
camps.name: Big-tech deals
camps.sub: A supply drop, not a lettered round
camps.story: Cloud giants invested in exchange for Anthropic running on their computing power. Amazon later added another $4B.
camps.play: A strategic investment comes from a big company that benefits from the startup’s success, often paid partly in services rather than plain cash.

camps.name: Series D
camps.story: Value more than quadrupled in under a year as businesses started paying for Claude.
camps.play: Series D and later rounds keep fuelling growth. Companies worth $10B+ are sometimes called decacorns.

camps.name: Series E
camps.story: The first round where Anthropic announced its valuation itself. Rounds are now measured in billions.
camps.play: Late-stage rounds bring in crossover funds, investors that buy both private and public stocks and help prepare for an IPO.

camps.name: Series F
camps.story: Microsoft and Nvidia pledged up to $15B combined two months later.
camps.play: When growth is this fast, rounds come months apart instead of years, each at a much higher price.

camps.name: Series G
camps.story: The second-largest private funding round ever at the time.
camps.play: At this size, sovereign wealth funds, the investment arms of national governments, become major backers.

camps.name: Series H
camps.story: A confidential draft of the IPO paperwork went to the SEC the following month.
camps.play: A final private round often sets a price benchmark just before going public.

camps.name: IPO
camps.lead: Underwriters: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley
camps.story: Public filing Oct 26, investor roadshow from Nov 10. 825M shares at $70–$78 on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with up to 20% set aside for everyday investors.
camps.play: To go public, banks underwrite the deal, the company files an S-1 disclosing its finances, pitches big investors on a roadshow, sets a share price and lists on an exchange.
